answer.evidence: Rows 5-11 form a light band with sheen streaks across the full 16px width. A dark front-edge line at row 12 ends it, and a second dark row at 13 (seen at x=8) acts as eave shadow. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small one-tile appliance with 12 visible tones per tile. That is within the reference range (hedge 9, cheese stall 17, roofed well 20) and above the thin lamp and bench, which measure 0. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The body shows about 5 grey/white steps, with highlight and shadow edges, a round door ring and a glass interior, plus a control panel. The dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, which on its own reads as near_black. But the material is itself neutral grey/white, so the dark edge is the dark tone of that material, not a pure-black sticker line. The lamp-crook reference has the same neutral edge. The edge is also not uniform around every shape, so I call it mixed. The piece is small and simple but is not thinner or flatter than the references of the same kind, so a careful artist would accept it next to them.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small light-grey box with a round porthole door and a control strip. The body reads as roughly 4 lightness steps (white highlight, light grey, mid grey, dark grey), compared with about 5-6 on the hedge, stall and well references. The outline is a fairly uniform dark line around the whole silhouette. 100% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so there is no tinted lean toward the adjacent material. That gives the shallow sticker look. Only the lamp-crook reference shares this 100% neutral figure, and the hedge, stall and well references have tinted or mixed edges. Density is acceptable by the numbers: 12 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge and 17-20 for the stall and well. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills, but the texture is limited to a few porthole and panel details. The body has no speckle, grain or per-part shading like the references. It reads thinner and more sticker-like than the references, so it fails on the neutral outline and the shallower ramp.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small grey and white washer with a round porthole door and a control strip. It carries about 4 grey lightness steps on the body and a few blue-grey steps on the glass, against about 5-6 per material on the references. The measured facts are fine on density: 12 visible tones per tile (hedge 9, cheese stall 17, well 20) and 0% near-flat coverage. The outline is the problem. 100% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so it is a uniform dark grey/black line around the whole silhouette. That is the sticker look. The hedge, cheese stall and well use tinted outlines (0-33% neutral), so they separate forms by value and material tone. The body is mostly smooth panels with little grain, speckle or per-part shading, so the machine looks flatter and thinner than the stall and well beside it. Shading depth and texture also fall slightly short of the references. A careful artist would not accept it next to them without tinting the outline and adding surface texture.
